source.title: Rapid Convergence of the Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm: Isoperimetry Suffices

checks.paper_location: Official proceedings main PDF and supplemental archive
checks.claim: The official supplement contains the complete 29-page camera-ready PDF, including Appendices B.2.1 and B.2.2.
checks.note: The archive member is langevin_neurips_camera_ready.pdf. Appendix pages 16-19 were inspected and agree with the author-hosted full version at https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/wibisono/VW19.pdf. The official supplement is a ZIP, not a standalone Supplemental.pdf.

checks.paper_location: Sections 2.1-2.2, equations (1)-(4), pages 3-4
checks.claim: The LSI normalization is \(2\alpha H_\nu(\rho)\le J_\nu(\rho)\).
checks.note: The code uses actual extended KL and the squared relative score. For normalized \(\rho=r\nu\), KL is identified with \(\int r\log r\,d\nu\). The endpoint retains separate finiteness proofs; the total real-conversion aliases alone do not express finiteness.

checks.paper_location: Section 2.2, equations (2) and (4), page 4
checks.claim: The functional inequality applies to density tests.
checks.note: IsLogSobolev tests strictly positive \(C^1\) relative probability densities. Its normalization matches the source, but equivalence with the full smooth-function formulation and extension by approximation are not proved. The endpoint supplies paths in this restricted class explicitly.

checks.paper_location: Section 3, equation (11); Appendix B.2.1, equations (28)-(29), pages 5 and 17
checks.claim: \(X_t=X_0-t\nabla U(X_0)+\sqrt{2t}\,Z\), with independent \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\).
checks.note: The actual measure update is the pushforward of the independent product of the current law and stdGaussian. Zero-time and step-endpoint identities are proved, with \(n=\operatorname{finrank}_{\mathbb R}E\). InterpolationDensity.lean additionally constructs the explicit positive-time Gaussian mixture and Gibbs-relative density, with actual-law identification. The entropy weak equation remains separate.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, after equation (33), page 19
checks.claim: \(\mathbb E\lVert X_t-X_0\rVert^2=t^2\mathbb E\lVert\nabla U(X_0)\rVert^2+2tn\).
checks.note: The proof checks the standard Gaussian second moment, zero mean, independent-product cross-term cancellation, and square integrability. It requires a finite squared-gradient moment, not a second moment of \(X_0\). Dimension zero is included.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, Gaussian interpolation preceding equation (30), pages 17-18
checks.claim: At every positive time the actual Gaussian interpolation has the explicit positive finite Gaussian mixture density and its normalized Gibbs-relative density.
checks.note: Tonelli and the already verified fixed-state Gaussian density identify the actual law with the mixture q_t. Each mixture value is strictly positive and bounded by the Gaussian normalizer. Dominated convergence proves spatial continuity. Probability normalization yields finite Gibbs partition, and cancellation of Z exp(U) against the target density identifies r_t ν with the actual law and proves normalization. Spatial C¹ regularity, time derivatives, entropy integrability/domination and entropy weak-test admissibility are not established by this construction.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, entropy calculation preceding equation (32), page 18
checks.claim: Density differentiation and integration by parts produce the entropy derivative.
checks.note: The derivative is derived from LocalEntropyRegularity, rather than assumed by the stronger wrapper. These data explicitly require local domination, integrability, measurability, and pointwise time derivatives; constructing them for the actual frozen-drift densities remains open. The existing endpoint still asks for two-sided local regularity including time zero. InteriorEntropy.lean separately proves actual-KL differentiation from local data only at positive times and a scalar comparison needing only interior derivatives and endpoint continuity. Those alternatives are not yet assembled into a broader initial-law endpoint.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equations (30)-(32), page 18
checks.claim: The frozen-drift equation determines entropy production.
checks.note: The code proves the score identities and tests an admissible forced weak equation with \(\log r+1\). That weak equation is an input for all \(C^1\) tests with the displayed integrable terms. Its validity for the actual law, including this noncompact entropy test, is not inferred from compact-test identities.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, integrating-factor entropy comparison, pages 18-19
checks.claim: The affine scalar entropy comparison requires derivatives only in the open interval and continuity at the endpoints.
checks.note: affine_decay_of_deriv_le_interior proves monotonicity of exp(at)(H(t)-b/a) from its nonpositive interior derivative, then evaluates at the endpoints. A separate theorem identifies actual-KL derivatives from LocalEntropyRegularity only on 0<t<T. The existing ULA endpoint still uses its previous closed-interval regularity interface; the new interior route does not by itself supply entropy continuity at zero or enlarge the endpoint theorem.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equation (33), page 18
checks.claim: Young's inequality leaves the Fisher coefficient \(-3/4\).
checks.note: The weighted cross term is proved integrable from its measurability and the two energy integrals. The estimate is \(H'\le-3J/4+\mathcal E\), with the same sign and coefficient as the source.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equation (33) and its following displacement calculation, pages 18-19
checks.claim: The joint gradient-error energy is bounded by \(L^2\) times displacement energy.
checks.note: frozen_gradient_error_energy proves integrability and the bound \(L^2(t^2G_0+2tn)\) on the actual independent product law. No drift-error estimate is assumed by that lemma.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equations (31)-(33), page 18
checks.claim: The entropy cross term can be evaluated under the joint law of \(X_0\) and \(X_t\).
checks.note: ConditionalDrift.lean constructs a strongly measurable state-space conditional mean by Doob–Dynkin factorization of the joint Gaussian discrepancy. Conditional Jensen transfers its squared energy, and set-integral and integrable inner-product identities identify its flux with the joint discrepancy flux. exists_frozen_drift_error_of_density gives the exact density-weighted bound. These results discharge conditional-mean existence, flux transfer, and Jensen; the actual interpolation PDE and admissibility of its entropy test remain separate.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, Lemma 9, page 16
checks.claim: \(\mathbb E_\nu\lVert\nabla U\rVert^2\le nL\).
checks.note: The shared theorem integral_norm_sq_gradient_gibbs_le proves this target bound under differentiability, gradient Lipschitzness, and a finite partition. Its proof uses translation invariance and a sub-Gaussian score estimate, rather than the source Hessian and integration-by-parts argument. memLp_gradient_gibbsMeasure supplies square integrability. GradientMoment.lean now combines these results with a finite-cost coupling to derive first-marginal gradient integrability and its transport-based moment bound. LSI-to-Talagrand is still needed for the entropy-cost estimate.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, Lemmas 9-10, pages 16-17; Section 2.2.1
checks.claim: \(G_\rho\le(4L^2/\alpha)H_\nu(\rho)+2nL\).
checks.note: GradientMoment.lean proves gradient square integrability and Gμ ≤ 2L² cost(c) + 2nL for a finite-cost coupling c with the normalized Gibbs target. The exact coefficient 4L²/α follows from an explicitly supplied cost(c) ≤ 2 KL/α. Thus the coupling-to-moment calculation is now proved. The LSI-to-Talagrand implication and the construction/approximation of a suitable entropy-cost coupling remain open. The existing ULA endpoint still retains its explicit hgradient and integrability inputs.

checks.paper_location: Section 3.1, Lemma 3 and Theorem 2; end of Appendix B.2.1 and Appendix B.2.2, pages 6 and 19
checks.claim: The step restriction is \(0<h\le\alpha/(4L^2)\).
checks.note: The displayed step restriction matches. The code additionally exposes \(\alpha\le L\) as hαL and requires positive \(L\). The appendix uses \(\alpha\le L\) to justify auxiliary small-step bounds but does not give a derivation there. Its derivation is not exported by the Lean development.

checks.paper_location: Section 3.1, Lemma 3, equation (12); Appendix B.2.1, final scalar calculation, pages 6 and 19
checks.claim: \(H(h)\le e^{-\alpha h}H(0)+6h^2nL^2\).
checks.note: The conclusion and step constants match. Lean sets \(A=(4L^2/\alpha)H(0)+2nL\) and obtains uniform forcing \(b=(\alpha/4)H(0)+(5/2)hnL^2\). Exact affine comparison with \(a=3\alpha/2\), \((1-e^{-ah})/a\le h\), and \(e^{-3x/2}+x/4\le e^{-x}\), where \(x=\alpha h\), give the stronger noise coefficient \(5/2\) before relaxing it to \(6\). The source instead uses a \(3hnL^2\) forcing term, an integrating factor, \(e^c\le1+2c\), and multiplicative exponential absorption.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.2, first displayed bound, page 19
checks.claim: Iteration yields \(H_k\le e^{-\alpha hk}H_0+8hnL^2/\alpha\).
checks.note: The scalar recurrence is iterated using the existing affine recurrence lemmas. The exact helper also retains the finite-horizon factor \(1-e^{-\alpha hk}\). The final constant \(8\) follows from \(1-e^{-x}\ge3x/4\) for \(0\le x\le1/4\). Lean proves that denominator estimate from \(e^x\ge1+x\) and a reciprocal bound.

checks.paper_location: Section 3.1, Theorem 2, page 6
checks.claim: The published conclusion concerns the actual ULA laws.
checks.note: The endpoint concerns actual Gaussian ULA laws and actual KL; it does not assume the discrete recurrence. It requires a differentiable potential, gradient Lipschitzness, LSI, α ≤ L and explicit analytic interpolation inputs. New modules construct positive-time densities and conditional drift, and derive the moment bound from an entropy-cost coupling. They do not yet establish the full density regularity, endpoint entropy continuity, admissible weak equation, LSI-to-Talagrand step or α ≤ L from the published assumptions. The original endpoint interface is unchanged, so this is not yet Theorem 2 from only LSI and smoothness.

checks.paper_location: Sections 2.1 and 3.1; Theorem 2 and Appendix B.2.2, pages 3, 6 and 19
checks.claim: Gaussian initialization is an example; the theorem also states an accuracy threshold.
checks.note: The initial law is an arbitrary probability law satisfying the explicit path and moment assumptions; it is not required to be Gaussian. Finite initial KL follows from the identified density at time zero. The separate logarithmic iteration threshold for a requested \(\delta\), and the stationary-bias corollary, are not exported as LSI theorems.

checks.paper_location: Section 2.3.1, Theorem 1; Appendix B.1.3, pages 5 and 16
checks.claim: Continuous Langevin entropy decays at rate \(2\alpha\).
checks.note: The continuous-time comparison uses \(e^{-2\alpha t}\), distinct from the discrete factor \(e^{-\alpha hk}\). EntropyFlow derives actual-KL decay given an admissible density path and an explicit dissipation identity; it does not construct a Langevin SDE law or prove Talagrand's inequality.

verdict: The formalized normalization, actual Gaussian update, explicit positive continuous finite mixture and Gibbs-relative densities, displacement and conditional drift energy/flux bridges, one-step constant 6, and iterated constant 8 agree with the 2019 reference. The coupling-to-gradient-moment calculation and a comparison using only interior derivatives are also proved. The actual-law endpoint remains conditional: C¹/time density regularity and entropy domination, endpoint entropy continuity, the admissible weak entropy equation, LSI-to-Talagrand transport control, and α ≤ L have not all been derived from LSI and smoothness alone.
